name: JUring
workload: Random-offset file reads/writes with 512B-64KB buffers at 1/8/20/25 concurrent threads, queue depth 256, measured with JMH
claimed_speedup: up to 489% faster reads at 4KB buffers vs pre-opened FileChannels; 231% faster single-thread 4KB writes (860 ops/ms vs 260 ops/ms); advantage shrinks and reverses slightly (-2%) at 20+ threads
tradeoffs: Java bindings over Linux io_uring via JNI/FFI; advantage diminishes/reverses at high thread counts (20+); early-stage per author's own admission
caveats: First-party README benchmark; no CPU model or JVM/compiler flags stated, only JMH methodology (buffer sizes, thread counts, queue depth); capped at C because hardware is unstated
found_via: HN Algolia search 'juring java' -> Show HN: JUring - Java bindings for io_uring file I/O (Jan 2025), covered by Phoronix Jan 14 2025

name: Apache Iggy (thread-per-core io_uring backend, v0.7.0)
baseline: epoll (via Tokio, as used in Iggy v0.5.0)
workload: Message streaming produce/consume benchmarks (iggy-bench) at 32 producers x 32 streams, 80GB/80M messages, and fsync-enabled 32-partition runs, comparing Iggy v0.5.0 (Tokio/epoll) vs v0.7.0 (thread-per-core io_uring)
claimed_speedup: P95 latency 3.77ms -> 1.62ms (+57%), P99 4.52ms -> 1.82ms (+60%), P999 5.43ms -> 2.38ms (+56%), P9999 27.52ms -> 11.83ms (+57%); fsync throughput 931 -> 1102 MB/s (+18%) with P95 33.98ms -> 18.49ms (+46%); raw throughput roughly unchanged (~1000 MB/s)
tradeoffs: Thread-per-core io_uring rewrite changes internal architecture; raw throughput similar to prior epoll version, gains are in tail latency not headline throughput
caveats: First-party engineering blog post; interactive benchmark dashboards are linked (benchmarks.iggy.apache.org) but are JS-rendered and did not yield CPU/OS/compiler details on fetch, so hardware/compiler fields are unconfirmed and tier is capped at C rather than A/B
found_via: HN Algolia search 'thread-per-core rust io_uring' -> 'Apache Iggy: thread-per-core with io_uring in Rust' blog (iggy.apache.org, Feb 27 2026)
